q: A Shuffle run starts but many fields arrive as empty strings. What should the workflow inspect first?
options: The production deployment of the associated endpoint agent
The description of the last operator who edited the canvas
The count of completed actions in unrelated executions
The input contract and the validation action's actual inputs
explanation: A run can start correctly while its contents fail validation.

q: What is the relationship between trigger and starting action?
options: Both are independent actions that always produce separate case records
The starting action always runs only after the workflow has finished
The trigger initiates the run; the action first processes its input
The trigger is a final result that confirms the approved effect
explanation: They describe initiation and the first executed operation respectively.

q: Two branches both create a case when a high-priority device lacks a known owner. What change fits the design?
options: Keep both writers and ask the incoming shift to remove duplicates
Use one case-writing step and merge contextual results
Delete every high-priority event with unresolved owner information
Make the case subject identical so two records count as one
explanation: One effect owner and explicit branching help prevent duplicate drafts.

q: What should an inventory lookup receive in the fictional example?
options: Only the approved asset identifier and necessary context
The original email attachments and every recipient's profile
The credentials used to browse the workflow's complete history
A second copy of the trigger regardless of what the lookup needs
explanation: Minimal inputs keep behaviour and permissions easier to review.

q: The condition sees the literal text false instead of a Boolean. What is a robust branch design?
options: Assume any nonempty field means the original condition was approved
Treat the incoming record's display label as an authorisation token
Choose whichever branch has run most successfully for past inputs
Test states and types explicitly before permitting the operation
explanation: Loose comparisons can treat unexpected data as a permitted value.

q: Why record the saved workflow revision with a test run?
options: To give all past executions the newest set of steps retroactively
To replace the need for a stable identifier on each input record
To identify the configuration that produced the result
To make the outcome depend on the canvas colour scheme
explanation: Saved revisions let reviewers connect evidence to the actual executed configuration.

q: The new draft names the wrong team although the lookup returned the right owner. Which step deserves inspection first?
options: The source alert's ordering relative to a totally unrelated case
The mapping from lookup output to the draft fields
The network configuration of the user's endpoint after the incident
The version of the original mail client that displayed the alert
explanation: Trace the last known correct value through the next transformation.

q: What makes a skipped action expected in run history?
options: Its recorded condition did not apply to that execution
An operator deleted it from the originally saved version afterward
The action's visible label matched an unrelated app name
A second event used the same asset ID during a different shift
explanation: Skipping can be a correct branch outcome with a reviewable reason.

q: A valid identifier is absent from the training inventory. How should this differ from invalid syntax?
options: Always drop the input because a known owner is mandatory in every workflow
Rewrite the incoming identifier to the nearest familiar value
Treat an unresolved owner as evidence that the original event is false
Record unresolved context while processing the valid input according to policy
explanation: Valid source data and missing enrichment present distinct conditions.

q: Which field belongs in reviewed workflow configuration?
options: A user-supplied title arriving in the current trigger record
The time of the most recent event to appear in the worksheet
The approved destination queue for normal case drafts
The sender display name copied from one suspicious message
explanation: Configuration owns stable operating boundaries rather than input-specific data.

q: A duplicate arrives before the first case draft becomes visible. What must the regression check demonstrate?
options: The engine reports at least one successful colour status
Only one effect survives the overlapping requests
The duplicate is always delivered after the initial run finishes
Each run generates a new case title sorted by receipt time
explanation: Concurrency can cause duplicates without an authoritative identity check.

q: What should the execution history let a reviewer inspect?
options: Run input reference, actions taken and the resulting state
Only the number of users allowed to edit the canvas
The names of all unrelated incidents managed by the team
A list of saved workflows with no connection to specific runs
explanation: Run-level evidence allows reconstruction of the particular result.

q: A timeout left a draft task possibly created. What is the prudent next route?
options: Repeat the full workflow and use whichever task ID appears latest
Declare the task never existed because the execution view lacks a result
Remove the original input and create a new record solely to bypass the retry check
Check the existing effect through its stable case key
explanation: A missing receipt is uncertainty about the effect rather than proof of absence.

q: What result is expected from a missing event identifier?
options: A new draft using the latest unrelated event ID
A silent dismissal that leaves no evidence of receipt
A review result without a guessed case draft
An automatic retry that adds the device ID as a synthetic event
explanation: Invalid source identity should stop the effect and remain reviewable.

q: A connector fails before completing an owner lookup. What should a workflow report?
options: The asset was confirmed not registered by the directory
Lookup unavailable, with an explicit owner follow-up
The event belongs to the last known owner for any prior asset
The alert no longer needs case review because enrichment failed
explanation: Failure to complete a search is different from a negative result.

q: What is the lab's recommended source for test data?
options: A small manual record with fictional values
An unreviewed export of real employee data
A live connector that can contact production targets
A public workflow trigger accepting unrelated inputs
explanation: A controlled fixture lets students predict and verify each branch safely.

q: What should be checked when a static setting and an input field have similar names?
options: The input automatically overrides the setting if it arrived more recently
Both sources can freely select credentials in any connected account
The workflow uses whichever field has the longer current value
Only reviewed settings determine permitted destinations and scope
explanation: Separating configuration from run input protects the approved boundary.

q: Why give the synthetic run sheet a test key?
options: To supersede the case system's official object identifier
To let the second reviewer publish an unrelated saved workflow
To connect the input, expected outcome and observed run
To hide whether other operators worked on the same fixture
explanation: A stable test reference makes outcome comparison reproducible.

q: A workflow change alters the interpretation of existing IDs. Which review prevents unexpected merges?
options: Allow every format by converting all incoming IDs to the same number
Test older and newer formats under the stated mapping contract
Ignore earlier records once the new version can be saved
Use names instead of identifiers for prior and current assets
explanation: Compatibility tests show whether different records still retain their identity.

q: What is the appropriate effect of a paper workflow's draft action?
options: A local text result for review
A remote device policy change requiring production authority
A real case notification sent through an external connector
An automatic permission grant to every role in the exercise
explanation: The paper design demonstrates workflow reasoning without real side effects.

q: A run waits at a manual decision. How is that distinct from an integration failure?
options: The workflow engine has already applied every downstream change
The source failed to deliver an event so there is no case context
The action must be retried immediately to bypass the pause
The step is intentionally pending with an owner and next action
explanation: A well-designed wait state records the dependency and who can resolve it.

q: What validates a route through the canvas in practice?
options: A screenshot made before the version being tested was saved
The number of connectors in the approved architecture diagram
The observed branch decisions and output for the saved run
A code comment explaining that every result should be valid
explanation: Execution evidence should match the specified path and case effect.

q: The same valid test now generates a draft with an omitted source reference. What is the correct response?
options: Accept it because the run succeeds and the owner field is present
Treat it as a regression in traceability and fix the mapping
Rewrite the original fixture's alert so it never had a source ID
Compare only event counts so missing fields cannot cause a mismatch
explanation: A successful run is only useful if its output meets the contract.

q: Which objective should a permissions review address?
options: Keep test, authoring and operational authority appropriately scoped
Give every draft viewer the ability to edit live connections
Store all reusable secrets in the case handoff for convenience
Permit one action to operate on every environment by default
explanation: Permissions should follow the role and authorised operating purpose.

q: What is the point of comparing the same fixture across revisions?
options: Make each version test only its easiest branch
Use separate synthetic input types so comparisons cannot overlap
Confirm that all dashboards have the same visual design
Verify intended differences against a stable input
explanation: Holding the fixture stable makes actual behaviour changes easier to identify.
